rules.sentence: For research purposes and to establish certain inclusive and exclusive criteria for the diagnosis of Alzheimer disease, a working group of the National Institute of Neurological and Communicative Disorders and Stroke (NINCDS) and the Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Diseases Association (ADRDA) in the past proposed the following criteria: (1) dementia defined by clinical examination, the Mini-Mental Scale, the Blessed Dementia Scale, or similar mental status examination—currently the Alzheimer Disease Assessment Scale (ADAS, which has 2 components, 1 for cognition, ADAS-cog and the other for activities of daily living, ADAS-ADL) is often used; (2) patient older than age 40 years; (3) deficits in 2 or more areas of cognition and progressive worsening of memory and other cognitive functions, such as language, perception, and motor skills (praxis); (4) absence of disturbed consciousness; and (5) exclusion of other brain diseases (McKhann et al, 1984; Tierney et al, 1988).

rules.sentence: Alzheimer disease is a neurodegenerative disease that causes progressive and disabling impairment of cognitive functions including memory, comprehension, language, attention, reasoning, and judgment.

rules.sentence: Onset before 65 years of age (early onset) is unusual and seen in less than 10% of Alzheimer disease patients.

rules.sentence: The most common presenting symptom is selective short-term memory loss.
rules._title: Provisional Mortality Data - United States, 2022. > Introduction

rules.sentence: The disease is invariably progressive, eventually leading to severe cognitive decline.

rules.sentence: Alzheimer disease is classified into preclinical, mild, moderate, and late-stage depending on the degree of cognitive impairment.

rules.sentence: The initial presenting symptom is usually recent memory loss with relative sparing of long-term memory and can be elicited in most patients even when not the presenting symptom.
rules._title: Provisional Mortality Data - United States, 2022. > Introduction

rules.sentence: Short-term memory impairment is followed by impairment in problem-solving, judgment, executive functioning, lack of motivation and disorganization, leading to problems with multitasking and abstract thinking.

rules._title: Provisional Mortality Data - United States, 2022. > Introduction

rules.sentence: Neuropsychiatric symptoms like apathy, social withdrawal, disinhibition, agitation, psychosis, and wandering are also common in mid to late stages.
rules._title: Provisional Mortality Data - United States, 2022. > Introduction

rules.sentence: Difficulty performing learned motor tasks (dyspraxia), olfactory dysfunction, sleep disturbances, extrapyramidal motor signs like dystonia, akathisia, and parkinsonian symptoms occur late in the disease.

rules._title: [Epidemiology and Clinical Presentation of Sarcoidosis]. > Differential Diagnosis

rules.sentence: Constrictive pericarditis (CP) is the most commonly mistaken for restrictive cardiomyopathy (RCM) out of the list above.
rules._title: [Epidemiology and Clinical Presentation of Sarcoidosis]. > Differential Diagnosis

rules.sentence: Juglar venous distension, Kussmaul sign, and diastolic sounds are both seen in RCM and CP.
rules._title: [Epidemiology and Clinical Presentation of Sarcoidosis]. > Differential Diagnosis

rules.sentence: However, there are some subtle differences.
rules._title: [Epidemiology and Clinical Presentation of Sarcoidosis]. > Differential Diagnosis

rules.sentence: For example, S3 and elevated BNP are far more common in RCM.
rules._title: [Epidemiology and Clinical Presentation of Sarcoidosis]. > Differential Diagnosis

rules.sentence: Whereas a pericardial knock, pericardial calcifications on chest x-ray, pericardial thickening on imaging, and BNP levels less than 100 are more likely seen in constrictive pericarditis.
rules._title: [Epidemiology and Clinical Presentation of Sarcoidosis]. > Differential Diagnosis

rules.sentence: Furthermore, one clear difference between the two diseases is the presence of ventricular interdependence.
rules._title: [Epidemiology and Clinical Presentation of Sarcoidosis]. > Differential Diagnosis

rules.sentence: Ventricular dependence seen only in CP is described as an increased filling of one of the ventricles only, with a reciprocal decreased filling of the other ventricle.[20]

rules.sentence: Darier disease, previously known as keratosis follicularis, is a rare autosomal dominant genodermatosis characterized by keratotic papules and longitudinal eyrthronychia; it is caused by mutations in the ATP2A2 gene, encoding a calcium pump within the endoplasmic reticulum.

rules.sentence: Seborrheic dermatitis occurs in 3% of the general population and in up to 50% of patients with HIV infection.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Seborrheic dermatitis increases in prevalence and severity as the CD4+ T cell count declines.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: In HIV-infected patients, seborrheic dermatitis may be aggravated by concomitant infection with Pityrosporum, a yeastlike fungus; use of topical antifungal agents has been recommended in cases refractory to standard topical treatment.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Folliculitis is among the most prevalent dermatologic disorders in patients with HIV infection and is seen in ~20% of patients.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: It is more common in patients with CD4+ T cell counts <200 cells/μL.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Eosinophilic pustular folliculitis is a rare form of folliculitis that is seen with increased frequency in patients with HIV infection.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: It presents as multiple, urticarial perifollicular papules that may coalesce into plaquelike lesions.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Skin biopsy reveals an eosinophilic infiltrate of the hair follicle, which in certain cases has been associated with the presence of a mite.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Patients typically have an elevated serum IgE level and may respond to treatment with topical anthelmintics.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Pruritus is a common symptom in patients with HIV infection and can lead to prurigo nodularis.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Patients with HIV infection have also been reported to develop a severe form of Norwegian scabies with hyperkeratotic psoriasiform lesions.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: The dermis contains mixed inflammatory cell infiltrates of lymphocytes, plasma cells, and eosinophils (see Image. Tungiasis Histology).[13]
rules._title: Overview of flea allergy dermatitis. > Histopathology

rules.sentence: The histopathologic pattern in papular urticaria consists of mild subepidermal edema, extravasation of erythrocytes, interstitial eosinophils, and exocytosis of lymphocytes.
rules._title: Overview of flea allergy dermatitis. > Histopathology

rules.sentence: When evaluating a patient suspected of flea bites, the provider should ask about living conditions, recent exposures, and similar symptoms in co-habitants.
rules._title: Overview of flea allergy dermatitis. > Histopathology

rules.sentence: The physical exam should include a thorough skin examination, particularly of exposed areas such as the arms, legs, upper back, and scalp.
rules._title: Overview of flea allergy dermatitis. > Histopathology

rules.sentence: Infested animals that have been handled or groomed may impact other body regions.
rules._title: Overview of flea allergy dermatitis. > Histopathology

rules.sentence: Patients with flea allergies frequently experience adverse reactions to various flea species.
rules._title: Overview of flea allergy dermatitis. > Histopathology

rules.sentence: Additionally, the exam should pursue details regarding any rashes, including duration, edema, erythema, and pruritus.
rules._title: Overview of flea allergy dermatitis. > Histopathology

rules.sentence: Evaluation for local areas of infection, while a rare presentation, should be performed as with all skin breaks.
rules._title: Overview of flea allergy dermatitis. > Histopathology

rules.sentence: Sharply demarcated grouped follicular papules on an erythematous base are commonly found on the extensor elbows, knees, Achilles tendon, and other bony prominences.

rules.sentence: Follicular papules may be variably scattered across other body areas.

rules.sentence: Griffiths described it in children in the first few years of life, with follicular hyperkeratosis, less prominent erythema, and occasional scleroderma-like changes of the hands.

rules.sentence: Griffiths and others have suggested that some Type V PRP cases may represent atypical follicular ichthyosis.[38]
rules._title: Pityriasis Rubra Pilaris. > History and Physical

rules.sentence: Spinal Epidural Abscess Spinal epidural abscess presents with midline back or neck pain, fever, and progressive limb weakness.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Aching pain is almost always present, either over the spine or in a radicular pattern.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: The duration of pain prior to presentation is generally ≤2 weeks but may on occasion be several months or longer.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Fever is typically but not invariably present, accompanied by elevated white blood cell count, sedimentation rate, and C-reactive protein.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: As the abscess expands, further spinal cord damage results from venous congestion and thrombosis.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Once weakness and other signs of myelopathy appear, progression may be rapid and irreversible.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Risk factors include an impaired immune status (HIV, diabetes mellitus, renal failure, alcoholism, malignancy), intravenous drug abuse, and infections of the skin or other tissues.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Two-thirds of epidural infections result from hematogenous spread of bacteria from the skin (furunculosis), soft tissue (pharyngeal or dental abscesses; sinusitis), or deep viscera (bacterial endocarditis).
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: The remainder arises from direct extension of a local infection to the subdural space; examples of local predisposing conditions are vertebral osteomyelitis, decubitus ulcers, lumbar puncture, epidural anesthesia, or spinal surgery.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Most cases are due to Staphylococcus aureus; gram-negative bacilli, Streptococcus, anaerobes, and fungi can also cause epidural abscesses.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Tuberculosis from an adjacent vertebral source (Pott’s disease) remains an important cause in the developing world.

rules.sentence: Most EGPA 1685 patients have asthma that arises later in life and in individuals who have no family history of atopy.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: The asthma can often be severe, and oral corticosteroids are often required to control symptoms but may lead to suppression of vasculitic symptoms.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: In addition to the more common symptoms of cough, dyspnea, sinusitis, and allergic rhinitis, alveolar hemorrhage and hemoptysis may also occur.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Over three-fourths of EGPA patients have neurologic manifestations.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Mononeuritis multiplex most commonly involves the peroneal nerve, but also involves the ulnar, radial, internal popliteal, and occasionally, cranial nerves.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Cerebral hemorrhage and infarction may also occur and are important causes of death.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Despite treatment, neurologic sequelae often do not completely resolve.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Approximately half of EGPA patients develop dermatologic manifestations.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: These include palpable purpura, skin nodules, urticarial rashes, and livedo.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Granulomas, vasculitis, and widespread myocardial damage may be found on biopsy or at autopsy, and cardiomyopathy and heart failure may be seen in up to half of all patients but are often at least partially reversible.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Acute pericarditis, constrictive pericarditis, myocardial infarction, and other electrocardiographic changes all may occur.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: The heart is a primary target organ in EGPA, and cardiac involvement often portends a worse prognosis.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: GI symptoms are common in EGPA and likely represent an eosinophilic gastroenteritis characterized by abdominal pain, diarrhea, GI bleeding, and colitis.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Ischemic bowel, pancreatitis, and cholecystitis have also been reported in association with EGPA and usually portend a worse prognosis.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Treatment Based on the response to the systemic vasculitides with ANCA activity, mononeuritis multiplex caused by vasculitis has been treated with corticosteroids and either rituximab 375 mg/m2 weekly for 4 weeks, or cyclophosphamide 1 g/m2 intravenously once a month for several months, but other equivalent regimens have been suggested.
rules._title: Neurology_Adams

rules.sentence: For the corticosteroid regimen, we have used intravenous methylprednisolone, 1.5 mg/kg, for several days, followed by oral corticosteroid treatment.
rules._title: Neurology_Adams

rules.sentence: It appears from clinical experience that corticosteroids alone are often inadequate, but some clinicians have taken this approach initially.
rules._title: Neurology_Adams

rules.sentence: Azathioprine is a reasonable alternative if cyclophosphamide is not tolerated.
rules._title: Neurology_Adams

rules.sentence: Treatment usually must be continued for at least several months.

rules.sentence: The diagnosis of this group of neuropathies rests on the finding of motor, reflex, and sensory changes confined to the territory of a single nerve; of several individual nerves affected in a random manner (mononeuritis or mononeuropathy multiplex); or of a plexus of nerves or part of a plexus (plexopathy).
rules._title: Neurology_Adams

rules.sentence: In addition to the signs of mononeuropathy multiplex, pain overlying the site of nerve infarction or distally is characteristic.
rules._title: Neurology_Adams

rules.sentence: The CSF protein is usually normal or slightly elevated, and in certain of these diseases there is a CSF pleocytosis (e.g., HIV, Lyme disease).
rules._title: Neurology_Adams

rules.sentence: Inflammatory neuropathy and the multifocal motor neuropathy caused by antibodies to GM1 also may be considered, because of their clinical similarity, in this group.

rules._title: Neurology_Adams

rules.sentence: Compressive radial mononeuropathy results after immobilization in an unnatural position, resulting in prolonged compressive damage to the radial nerve.
rules._title: Radial nerve palsy. > Epidemiology

rules.sentence: This palsy classically involves an individual falling asleep with the arm hanging over a chair or other hard surface, leading to compression within the axilla.
rules._title: Radial nerve palsy. > Epidemiology

rules.sentence: While these are the classically described presentations, one must be aware that compressive radial mononeuropathy can be caused by any unnatural positioning or use of the limbs that can cause compression by a similar mechanism.
rules._title: Radial nerve palsy. > Epidemiology

rules.sentence: Patients will often report symptom onset after consuming a large amount of alcohol and then sleeping in an unnatural position.
rules._title: Radial nerve palsy. > Epidemiology

rules.sentence: Otherwise, patients report some other mechanism by which compression would have been unnaturally placed on the upper medial arm or axilla.
rules._title: Radial nerve palsy. > Epidemiology

rules.sentence: It is possible that patients may not provide this info until prompted, as it can go unrecognized as an inciting event.
rules._title: Radial nerve palsy. > Epidemiology

rules.sentence: Symptoms can also begin several days after the initial insult, leading to a delayed presentation.
rules._title: Radial nerve palsy. > Epidemiology

rules.sentence: Patients may report numbness, weakness, tingling, pain, or any combination.
rules._title: Radial nerve palsy. > Epidemiology

rules.sentence: On physical exam, patients may demonstrate a characteristic wrist drop, which results from the loss of extensor muscle function controlled by the radial nerve branches and preservation of the flexor muscles controlled by other nerves in the hand and arm.
rules._title: Radial nerve palsy. > Epidemiology

rules.sentence: This leads to an inability to extend the wrist and fingers at the level of the metacarpophalangeal joints.
rules._title: Radial nerve palsy. > Epidemiology

rules.sentence: Patients also lose the ability to extend the thumb, resulting in difficulty opening the hand and grasping objects.
rules._title: Radial nerve palsy. > Epidemiology

rules.sentence: Providers should be aware that patients can still extend their fingers at the level of the proximal and distal interphalangeal joints, as the ulnar nerve controls these.
rules._title: Radial nerve palsy. > Epidemiology

rules.sentence: Additionally, patients may exhibit loss of the triceps reflex, which is controlled by radial nerve innervation.
rules._title: Radial nerve palsy. > Epidemiology

rules.sentence: Sensory deficits often involve the posterior or lateral upper arm, with symptoms extending distally to affect the posterior forearm, posterior hand, and posterolateral aspect of the lateral three-and-a-half digits.
rules._title: Radial nerve palsy. > Epidemiology

rules.sentence: Diabetic polyradiculopathy is a syndrome characterized by severe disabling pain in the distribution of one or more nerve roots.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: It may be accompanied by motor weakness.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Involvement of the lumbar plexus or femoral nerve may cause severe pain in the thigh or hip and may be associated with muscle weakness in the hip flexors or extensors (diabetic amyotrophy).
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Fortunately, diabetic polyradiculopathies are usually self-limited and resolve over 6–12 months.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Mononeuropathy (dysfunction of isolated cranial or peripheral nerves) is less common than polyneuropathy in DM and presents with pain and motor weakness in the distribution of a single nerve.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Involvement of the third cranial nerve is most common and is heralded by diplopia.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Physical examination reveals ptosis and ophthalmoplegia with normal pupillary constriction to light.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: DM-related autonomic neuropathy can involve multiple systems, including the cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, genitourinary, sudomotor, and metabolic systems.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Autonomic neuropathies affecting the cardiovascular system cause a resting tachycardia and orthostatic hypotension.
rules._title: InternalMed_Harrison

rules.sentence: Gastroparesis and bladder-emptying abnormalities are often caused by the autonomic neuropathy seen in DM (discussed below).

rules.sentence: Hyperhidrosis of the upper extremities and anhidrosis of the lower extremities result from sympathetic nervous system dysfunction.

rules.sentence: Anhidrosis of the feet can promote dry skin with cracking, which increases the risk of foot ulcers.

rules.sentence: Chronic RHF arises from primary RV dysfunction, which can manifest as an intrinsic impairment of contractility and/or lusitropy, or, more commonly, secondarily due to pressure or volume overload, often in the setting of left-sided HF (Table 1).

rules.sentence: Primary RV dysfunction can be attributed to etiologies such as myocardial infarction, myocarditis, cardiomyopathy, post-surgical states, or the presence of a left ventricular assist device.

rules.sentence: Secondary RV dysfunction resulting from pressure overload is caused by pre-capillary pulmonary hypertension, post- or combined pre-and post- capillary pulmonary hypertension (secondary to left HF), pulmonary embolism, various forms of lung disease, or pulmonary valve stenosis.

rules.sentence: Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia is an inherently unstable rhythm that either spontaneously terminates or degenerates into ventricular fibrillation, leading to cardiac arrest.
rules._title: Heart Disease and Stroke Statistics-2018 Update: A Report From the American Heart Association. > Issues of Concern

rules.sentence: Patients presenting with this rhythm may develop syncopal episodes, warranting the initiation of the unstable tachycardia algorithm.
rules._title: Heart Disease and Stroke Statistics-2018 Update: A Report From the American Heart Association. > Issues of Concern

rules.sentence: In rare instances when patients present with runs of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and remain stable, magnesium sulfate may be administered empirically as an IV bolus while efforts are made to identify and correct the underlying cause.
rules._title: Heart Disease and Stroke Statistics-2018 Update: A Report From the American Heart Association. > Issues of Concern

rules.sentence: Possible etiologies include electrolyte abnormalities that can lead to long QT syndrome; organic heart diseases, such as ischemia; genetic channelopathies, such as Brugada or short QT syndrome; and exercise-induced catecholaminergic ventricular tachycardia.
rules._title: Heart Disease and Stroke Statistics-2018 Update: A Report From the American Heart Association. > Issues of Concern

rules.sentence: Long QT-induced polymorphic ventricular tachycardia is managed emergently with magnesium sulfate given as a 2-g IV bolus, which may be repeated as long as hypermagnesemia is avoided.

rules.sentence: A rare type of congenital heart disease is an interrupted aortic arch (IAA), which affects approximately 1.5% of congenital heart disease patients.[4]
rules._title: Pulse Oximetry and Auscultation for Congenital Heart Disease Detection. > Introduction

rules.sentence: Interrupted aortic arch is an anomaly that can be considered the most severe form of aortic coarctation.[5]
rules._title: Pulse Oximetry and Auscultation for Congenital Heart Disease Detection. > Introduction

rules.sentence: In an IAA, there is an anatomical and luminal disruption between the ascending and descending aorta.
rules._title: Pulse Oximetry and Auscultation for Congenital Heart Disease Detection. > Introduction

rules.sentence: IAA is a ductus dependent lesion since this is the only way the blood flow can travel to places distal to the disruption.
rules._title: Pulse Oximetry and Auscultation for Congenital Heart Disease Detection. > Introduction

rules.sentence: There is posterior malalignment of the conal septum additional to the interrupted aortic arch, producing a ventricular septal defect as an associated lesion.
rules._title: Pulse Oximetry and Auscultation for Congenital Heart Disease Detection. > Introduction

rules.sentence: This lesion is present is approximately 73% of all cases.
rules._title: Pulse Oximetry and Auscultation for Congenital Heart Disease Detection. > Introduction

rules.sentence: Due to this malalignment, there could be left ventricular outflow tract obstruction.
rules._title: Pulse Oximetry and Auscultation for Congenital Heart Disease Detection. > Introduction

rules.sentence: Besides a ventricular septal defect, IAA can be associated with other more complicated cardiac anomalies; for example, transposition of the great arteries, truncus arteriosus, aortopulmonary window, single ventricle, aortic valve atresia, right-sided ductus, and double-outlet right ventricle.[4]

rules.sentence: Cyanotic congenital heart disease occurs when some of the systemic venous return crosses from the right side of the heart to the left and returns to the body without going through the lungs (righttoleft shunt).
rules._title: Pediatrics_Nelson

rules.sentence: Cyanosis, the visible sign of this shunt, occurs when approximately 5 g/100 mL of reduced hemoglobin is present in systemic blood.
rules._title: Pediatrics_Nelson

rules.sentence: Thus, a polycythemic patient appears cyanotic with a lower percentage of reduced hemoglobin.

rules.sentence: A patient with anemia requires a higher percentage of reduced hemoglobin for the recognition of cyanosis.
